question: Which food item is a well-known high choking hazard for toddlers?

options.A: Soft bananas
options.B: Whole grapes
options.C: Mashed potatoes
options.D: Cooked oatmeal

explanation: Round, firm foods like whole grapes can easily block a child's small airway and must be cut into small pieces. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h6)

question: What type of tasks are usually performed in sheltered workshops?

options.A: Complex corporate management and financial auditing
options.B: Simple manual tasks like packaging, craft-making, and sewing
options.C: Advanced software engineering and system architecture
options.D: Heavy construction and high-risk electrical wiring

explanation: The work is kept simple and safe so that participants with varying abilities can join in without getting hurt. Well done! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T7#GNS314_U5_T7_h3)

question: At what angle should an intramuscular injection be inserted into the skin?

options.A: 45 degrees
options.B: 90 degrees
options.C: 15 degrees
options.D: 30 degrees

explanation: A perpendicular 90-degree angle ensures the needle penetrates deep enough to reach the muscle layer beneath the skin and fat. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is a great benefit of using the vaginal route for misoprostol?

options.A: It works instantly in under five minutes
options.B: It means you don't need to know how far along the pregnancy is
options.C: It completely stops all cramping pain
options.D: It results in fewer gastrointestinal side effects like nausea

explanation: Vaginal use skips the stomach processing, which helps many patients avoid nasty stomach upset and vomiting. Smart clinical choice! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h4)

question: Why must you clean connection hubs with an alcohol swab before changing lines?

options.A: It ensures the plastic tubing remains soft and flexible
options.B: It makes the digital screen easier to read in bright light
options.C: It removes sticky residue left behind by medical tape
options.D: It prevents microbes from entering the bloodstream and causing infection

explanation: Spot on! Good aseptic technique keeps nasty bacteria from hitching a ride directly into your patient's bloodstream. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h7)

question: What is the primary risk of pouring liquid disinfectant directly onto a digital weighing scale?

options.A: Liquid can seep inside and damage internal electronic circuits
options.B: It permanently locks the zero-adjustment mechanism
options.C: It causes the exterior paint to change color immediately
options.D: It will make the metal platform slippery for the next patient

explanation: Moisture inside electronic devices causes short circuits and rust, so nurses should use damp disinfectant wipes rather than pouring liquid. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a good reason to avoid using leftover antibiotics for a new cold?

options.A: Colds are usually caused by viruses, which antibiotics cannot kill
options.B: Using leftover drugs can lead to incorrect dosing and drug resistance
options.C: Leftover antibiotics are guaranteed to work faster than fresh prescriptions
options.D: Sharing drugs promotes dangerous resistance patterns in the community

explanation: That's right! Leftover drugs are never a magic shortcut; using them wrongly for viral colds is useless and dangerous. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is a classic example of indirect contact transmission?

options.A: A nurse catches scabies after handling a patient without gloves
options.B: A farmer develops a hookworm infection walking barefoot in soil
options.C: A baby gets pinkeye (conjunctivitis) from touching a contaminated toy
options.D: A student inhales droplet nuclei from a classmate coughing

explanation: Spot on! Indirect contact happens when you pick up germs from an object (like a toy) rather than touching an infected person directly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h1)

question: A nurse reads a study and wonders if the results can safely apply to patients in her own local hospital. Which concept is she checking?

options.A: External validity
options.B: Intervention bias
options.C: Instrument reliability
options.D: Internal consistency

explanation: External validity is all about the real world. It asks: can we take these study results and successfully apply them to other patients outside the original study setting? [learn more](GNS224_U1_T1#GNS224_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is the main goal of disaster mitigation?

options.A: To completely eliminate all natural hazards on earth
options.B: To manage patients only after a disaster has occurred
options.C: To reduce the severity and impact of potential disasters
options.D: To provide immediate funding for post-disaster recovery

explanation: You've got this! Mitigation is all about lessening the damage from hazards that we cannot completely stop. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h1)

question: Why must school nurses also focus on non-communicable conditions like asthma?

options.A: Asthma attacks can spread rapidly from child to child
options.B: Children with asthma cannot participate in lessons at all
options.C: Non-communicable diseases are always caused by poor hygiene
options.D: These chronic conditions require daily management at school

explanation: Conditions like asthma require school staff to know emergency protocols, such as administering rescue inhalers when symptoms flare up. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is a key part of a safety plan made for someone who has experienced violence?

options.A: Quitting your job right away without any money saved
options.B: Confronting the abuser face-to-face in a public place
options.C: Knowing safe places to go and packing important documents
options.D: Avoiding all contact with healthcare workers and social workers

explanation: Well done! A practical safety plan helps someone leave quickly if danger gets worse, including knowing where to find shelter and keeping vital papers ready. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T14#GNS313_U3_T14_h6)

question: When would a nurse researcher choose a correlational design?

options.A: When studying a harmful habit where experimenting on humans is unethical
options.B: When testing a brand new surgical tool in the operating room
options.C: When proving that a specific drug cures a specific bacterial infection
options.D: When randomly assigning patients to receive different hospital diets

explanation: Exactly! When it's wrong or impossible to expose people to harmful conditions on purpose, we use correlational studies to observe safely instead. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T12#GNS224_U1_T12_h1)

question: An infant receives protective antibodies through breast milk. What type of immunity is this?

options.A: Natural active immunity
options.B: Artificial passive immunity
options.C: Artificial active immunity
options.D: Natural passive immunity

explanation: This is natural passive immunity because the mother's antibodies pass naturally to the baby to give temporary protection. [learn more](GST114_U4_T5#GST114_U4_T5_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of a community health monitoring framework?

options.A: To replace traditional bedside nursing documentation with digital spreadsheets
options.B: To serve as a blueprint guiding data flow, collection responsibilities, and reporting schedules
options.C: To secure permanent international funding without local community input
options.D: To punish health workers who fail to meet their monthly targets

explanation: Think of a monitoring framework as your roadmap—it guides everyone on what to measure, when to report, and who is in charge. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T21#GNS225_U2_T21_h4)

question: What happens right away if a food sample is collected poorly or transported in warm conditions?

options.A: The food sample automatically sterilizes itself
options.B: The laboratory test results become invalid
options.C: The sample gains extra vitamins and minerals
options.D: Pathogens instantly transform into harmless spores

explanation: That's correct! If food isn't kept cool during transport, bacteria will either multiply or die off, meaning the lab won't see the true picture of what was in the food. [learn more](GST114_U5_T5#GST114_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why must community nurses look beyond the clinic when dealing with poor nutrition?

options.A: Because nutrition problems only exist inside large hospital wards
options.B: Because hospital management forbids nurses from talking about food
options.C: Because clinical medications can cure malnutrition completely on their own
options.D: Because root causes like poverty and food disruption require community-based action

explanation: Spot on! Nutritional challenges are often tied to bigger social and economic issues. Giving medicine alone isn't enough—we need community action and education too. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h1)

question: Why is telehealth particularly helpful for patients living in remote rural areas?

options.A: It replaces the need for any electrical power in the home
options.B: It reduces the need to travel long distances for routine check-ins
options.C: It guarantees that patients will never need surgery
options.D: It makes prescription drugs free for everyone

explanation: Telehealth lets patients consult nurses and doctors remotely, saving travel time and expenses for those far from health facilities. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why are elderly patients especially prone to severe confusion during emergency evacuations?

options.A: They frequently lose essential sensory aids like glasses and hearing aids
options.B: They are naturally immune to psychological shock and trauma
options.C: They prefer to ignore instructions given by emergency staff
options.D: Their medical conditions prevent them from feeling fear

explanation: You nailed it! Losing glasses or hearing aids in a sudden rush cuts older adults off from their surroundings, making confusion and anxiety spike. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h5)

question: A patient with chronic kidney disease is given a synthetic form of erythropoietin. What is the main goal of this treatment?

options.A: Increase calcium absorption in the small intestine
options.B: Lower systemic blood pressure by dilating vessels
options.C: Help the kidneys filter urea and creatinine faster
options.D: Improve red blood cell count and reduce fatigue

explanation: Awesome job! This medication steps in to do the job of the missing natural hormone, signaling the bone marrow to make fresh red blood cells and give the patient their energy back. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which home change is most important for a patient who uses a wheelchair?

options.A: Removing all windows to improve ventilation
options.B: Widening doorways and installing access ramps
options.C: Replacing all tiled floors with thick carpets
options.D: Installing bright fluorescent lighting in every room

explanation: Wheelchair users need ramps to handle steps and widened doorways so they can move freely and safely from room to room. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h5)

question: A patient has a viral cough and cold. Why won't standard antibiotics help clear it up?

options.A: Viruses multiply too slowly for antibiotics to catch them in time
options.B: Viral agents are too large to be penetrated by oral medications
options.C: Antibiotics immediately destroy the white blood cells fighting the virus
options.D: Viruses lack the cellular structures that standard antibacterial drugs target

explanation: Antibiotics are built to attack bacteria (like destroying their cell walls). Since viruses are structured differently, antibiotics just can't touch them! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T78#GNS214_U1_T78_h2)

question: What is the main goal of Mass Drug Administration (MDA) programs in communities with high worm rates?

options.A: Reducing the overall parasite burden across the entire population
options.B: Eliminating the need for basic sanitation and clean water supply
options.C: Curating permanent immunity against all bacterial and viral pathogens
options.D: Diagnosing individual complex surgical emergencies in local hospitals

explanation: MDA treats whole communities at once to quickly bring down the total number of worms and stop heavy transmission without needing individual lab tests. [learn more](GST114_U3_T6#GST114_U3_T6_h9)

question: How does health care economics actually affect you as a nurse on the ward?

options.A: It removes all financial stress from the hospital
options.B: It stops nurses from ever using advanced equipment
options.C: It dictates how staff manage limited supplies and time
options.D: It determines the exact salary of every patient

explanation: Exactly! Every day on the ward, you live economics when juggling limited shifts, gloves, and medication supplies to give the best care possible. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h1)

question: Where are most private hospitals and well-equipped health facilities concentrated in Nigeria?

options.A: Isolated coastal fishing ports
options.B: Nomadic desert settlements
options.C: Urban centers and major cities
options.D: Remote rural farming villages

explanation: Private investors tend to set up where business is booming, meaning big cities get better equipped facilities than rural areas. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why must clean utility rooms be kept strictly separate from dirty utility spaces in a hospital?

options.A: To comply with financial auditing standards for medical supplies
options.B: To make it easier for patients to walk around the hospital corridors
options.C: To ensure that nurses can easily find their personal meal breaks
options.D: To prevent cross-contamination and control hospital-acquired infections

explanation: Keeping clean items far away from contaminated waste is a golden rule of infection control to keep our patients safe from nasty germs! [learn more](GST321_U4_T5#GST321_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why should a nurse adjust the weighing scale to zero before weighing every child?

options.A: To make the scale display readings in kilograms instead of pounds
options.B: To comply with international manufacturer warranties
options.C: To calm the child down before the measurement process begins
options.D: To prevent small errors from accumulating between readings

explanation: Always zeroing your scale clears any leftover weight from the previous patient, keeping your numbers accurate every time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h3)

question: What does equity in a healthcare budget mean?

options.A: Distributing health services fairly so vulnerable populations receive care
options.B: Giving every single department the exact same amount of cash
options.C: Allowing only wealthy patients to access specialized treatments
options.D: Ensuring the hospital makes a profit on every patient admitted

explanation: Budgetary equity focuses on fair distribution so that those in need, including vulnerable groups, can access care. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h2)

question: A community health nurse is planning a cervical cancer screening outreach. Which test is she most likely to utilize?

options.A: Liver biopsy
options.B: Chest X-ray
options.C: Pap smear
options.D: Prostate-specific antigen test

explanation: A Pap smear is a standard, widely used screening tool for detecting cervical cell abnormalities and precancerous lesions. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why can a severe, body-wide infection cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure?

options.A: The heart muscle suddenly stops beating with normal force
options.B: Widespread blood vessel dilation reduces systemic vascular resistance
options.C: The kidneys suddenly absorb all available fluid from the blood
options.D: Lungs take in too much oxygen and thin out the blood plasma

explanation: You got it! Severe inflammation makes blood vessels relax and widen all over the body, making it hard to keep blood pressure up. [learn more](GST114_U2_T4#GST114_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical concern when using connected monitoring devices?

options.A: Balancing constant safety tracking with the right to privacy
options.B: Guarantees that patient medical bills will always be cheaper
options.C: Making sure patients understand and consent to surveillance
options.D: Protecting wireless patient data from cyber security threats

explanation: Monitoring devices do not guarantee lower bills; privacy, security, and consent are the true ethical concerns. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which enzyme speeds up the breakdown of carbonic acid into water and carbon dioxide in the kidney tubules?

options.A: Amylase
options.B: Carbonic anhydrase
options.C: Aldosterone
options.D: Renin

explanation: Carbonic anhydrase is a super-helpful enzyme that acts like a matchmaker, quickly converting carbonic acid back and forth between water and carbon dioxide. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T12#GNS121_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why must nurses balance medical treatments with a resident's personal wishes?

options.A: To avoid documenting any clinical changes in the chart.
options.B: To ensure the patient performs all physical therapy alone.
options.C: To respect resident dignity while still achieving safe, effective outcomes.
options.D: To completely bypass hospital discharge regulations.

explanation: Person-centered care means we team up with our patients, respecting what they value while keeping them safe and healthy. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why is working together across different agencies so vital during a major public health emergency?

options.A: External security forces take complete legal ownership of medical patient charts
options.B: Government regulations mandate that all agencies merge into a single permanent ministry
options.C: No single agency has enough resources or personnel to handle a major disaster alone
options.D: It eliminates the need for nurses to perform clinical triage duties in hospitals

explanation: Disasters are too big for just one group. By combining health workers, security, and transport agencies, everyone pitches in to save lives. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h9)

question: How does buying fruits and vegetables in their natural season help a household manage its food budget?

options.A: Purchasing seasonal items prevents the need to cook meals
options.B: In-season produce is typically more abundant and therefore cheaper
options.C: Out-of-season crops always contain more vitamins
options.D: Seasonal foods require chemical preservatives to stay fresh

explanation: High local supply during harvest seasons drives down the cost of fruits and vegetables while maintaining high nutritional quality. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h3)

question: What is the main goal of using aseptic technique in the ward?

options.A: To prevent pathogen contamination during clinical procedures
options.B: To cure patients who already have active bacterial infections
options.C: To completely eliminate all microbes from the hospital environment
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of hospital-acquired illnesses

explanation: You've got this! Aseptic techniques are just safe practices we use to stop harmful germs from getting into clean or sterile parts of the body during procedures. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which chemical messenger (neurotransmitter) is released by almost all autonomic preganglionic nerve fibers?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Norepinephrine

explanation: Acetylcholine is the go-to chemical messenger used at the first synapse (ganglion) for both the sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions. Great job! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why are bedside nurses usually the best people to spot where clinical changes are needed?

options.A: They spend most of their shift working in the hospital administrative offices
options.B: They dictate national health policies and regulatory frameworks
options.C: They have final authority over hospital budget allocations
options.D: They experience daily workflows and spot operational bottlenecks firsthand

explanation: You are right at the bedside every day, so you see firsthand what slows things down or causes delays for patients. Who knows the ward better than you? [learn more](GST319_U3_T3#GST319_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why do nurses watch out specifically for waterborne diseases after heavy floods?

options.A: Excessive rainfall permanently destroys all local mosquito breeding grounds
options.B: Overflowing sewage systems mix with and contaminate drinking water sources
options.C: Damp weather conditions cause rapid airborne transmission of influenza
options.D: Standing water causes an immediate drop in local atmospheric oxygen levels

explanation: Floodwaters easily ruin sanitation systems, letting sewage leak into drinking water and spreading dangerous germs. Great to keep in mind for community health! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T6#GNS315_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the core question asked during a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) investigation?

options.A: Which specific staff member is guilty of negligence?
options.B: Why did the system allow this event to happen?
options.C: How much financial loss did the hospital suffer?
options.D: Who should be fired immediately for this failure?

explanation: RCA is like detective work for processes—we look for broken systems, not bad people. [learn more](GST319_U5_T4#GST319_U5_T4_h6)

question: When you turn your palm downward to type on a phone or keyboard, what is this movement called?

options.A: Elevation
options.B: Adduction
options.C: Supination
options.D: Pronation

explanation: Brilliant! Pronation turns the palm to face backward or downward, while supination turns it upward (like holding soup). [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h5)

question: An angry nursing student wants to yell at a strict clinical instructor, but instead channels that energy into scrubbing the skill lab for hours. What defense mechanism is this?

options.A: Sublimation
options.B: Projection
options.C: Regression
options.D: Denial

explanation: That is sublimation! It is taking raw, unacceptable aggression and turning it into something super productive and socially acceptable. Cleaning counts as a win! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T2#GNS314_U2_T2_h3)

question: When an artificial intelligence alert pops up on a patient monitor, what should the nurse do?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately based on the computer screen
options.B: Ignore the patient completely because the computer is always right
options.C: Turn off all hospital monitors so they stop making noise
options.D: Evaluate the alert and use clinical judgment to decide the next step

explanation: Technology is a support tool, and nurses must always apply their own professional assessment before taking action. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h6)

question: What should you do first if a bedside monitor shows a sudden drop in oxygen, but the patient looks calm and comfortable?

options.A: Turn off the alarm permanently so it stops annoying staff
options.B: Check the patient and the sensor placement on the finger
options.C: Call the doctor immediately to report a code blue
options.D: Assume the patient is dying and start chest compressions

explanation: Don't panic! Sensors often slip or wiggle loose. Always check your patient and the equipment first before jumping to conclusions. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h2)

question: When starting a 'less than' ogive on graph paper, where should your very first point land on the x-axis?

options.A: At the highest possible number recorded in the entire study
options.B: Right in the middle of the very last group listed
options.C: At the exact median value calculated for the sample
options.D: At the lower boundary of the first class where frequency is zero

explanation: That's it! We anchor our 'less than' ogive right at the starting line—the lower boundary of the first class where no data has piled up yet. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T11#GNS217_U4_T11_h4)

question: What is the primary role of information retrieval systems in evidence-based nursing?

options.A: Replacing doctors during emergency resuscitation procedures
options.B: Recording patient vital signs directly into paper charts
options.C: Scheduling nursing shifts for weekend hospital coverage
options.D: Connecting clinical questions to published research evidence

explanation: IR systems give nurses rapid access to the research literature needed to support evidence-based clinical decisions. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h7)

question: A head nurse wants to know if a newly introduced fall-prevention bundle actually decreases patient falls over the next year on the surgical ward. Which action represents applying prospective thinking?

options.A: Implementing the bundle today and tracking fall rates prospectively over the coming year
options.B: Interviewing staff nurses about falls that occurred before they were born
options.C: Asking elderly patients to guess why they might fall in the future
options.D: Looking up incident reports from five years ago to see how many people slipped

explanation: Applying a measure today and observing future outcomes embodies the core methodology of prospective clinical research. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h7)

question: Where is the safest site to give a routine intramuscular vaccine to a healthy baby?

options.A: Abdominal subcutaneous fat tissue
options.B: Vastus lateralis muscle in the thigh
options.C: Deltoid muscle in the upper arm
options.D: Dorsal gluteal muscle in the lower back

explanation: The thigh muscle (vastus lateralis) is well-developed in infants, making it the safest and easiest spot for their shots. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h5)

question: What is the typical pH range of normal human semen?
explanation: Semen is mildly alkaline to survive the acidic conditions of the vaginal tract. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why is the agricultural sector so important when health workers try to improve nutrition?

options.A: Because farming practices have no impact on community health outcomes
options.B: Because farmers are legally required to diagnose nutritional deficiencies
options.C: Because agricultural workers manage all rural health clinics
options.D: Because agriculture determines how much and what types of food are produced

explanation: Brilliant! Farming dictates what food is available and how varied the food supply is, making agriculture the very foundation of good nutrition. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h7)

question: How does a nurse show client-centered care when planning a patient's rehab?

options.A: Involving the client and family in setting realistic daily personal goals
options.B: Following a rigid hospital routine without considering individual preferences
options.C: Deciding the discharge schedule without asking the client about their home setup
options.D: Focusing solely on physical therapy exercises prescribed by the doctor

explanation: Client-centered care means the patient and their family are part of the team, not just bystanders. When goals matter to them, they work harder to reach them! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T2#GNS314_U5_T2_h2)

question: Which common food item must a patient avoid before doing a stool occult blood test?

options.A: Green tea
options.B: White rice
options.C: Red meat
options.D: Boiled yam

explanation: You nailed it! Red meat has hemoglobin that can mess with the test chemicals and give a false-positive result. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T5#GNS123_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is St. John's Wort most commonly used for?

options.A: Chronic high blood pressure
options.B: Mild to moderate depression
options.C: Bacterial respiratory infections
options.D: Severe acute schizophrenia

explanation: St. John's Wort is a popular herb often used to lift the mood in mild to moderate depression, kind of like a natural antidepressant. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T3#GNS314_U4_T3_h2)

question: What does direct calorimetry measure to determine energy expenditure?

options.A: Heat produced by the body
options.B: Carbon dioxide exhaled in breath
options.C: Oxygen inhaled through a mask
options.D: Nitrogen lost in urine samples

explanation: Direct calorimetry calculates energy use by measuring the actual heat given off by a person inside a special chamber. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h6)

question: How does Streptococcus usually arrange itself under a microscope?

options.A: In large flat sheets
options.B: In grape-like clusters
options.C: As single isolated squares
options.D: In chains of cells

explanation: Spot on! The prefix 'strepto-' means twisted chains, which helps you tell it apart from bacteria that grow in bunches. [learn more](GST114_U5_T3#GST114_U5_T3_h2)

question: About how many extra calories a day are needed in the later stages of pregnancy?

options.A: Three hundred calories
options.B: Two thousand calories
options.C: One thousand calories
options.D: Fifty calories

explanation: Spot on! An extra 300 calories a day—like a small, nourishing snack—is usually all it takes to fuel the final trimesters. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T008#GNS227_U2_T008_h2)

question: What can a patient do using a patient portal connected to a hospital EHR?

options.A: It allows patients to view lab results and message their care team online
options.B: It gives hospital administrators access to employee payroll records
options.C: It lets patients perform emergency surgical procedures on themselves
options.D: It replaces the physical bedside nurse during hospital admissions

explanation: Spot on! Patient portals empower patients to check their own lab results and chat with their nurses and doctors online. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h4)

question: In the famous Swiss Cheese Model of safety, what do the holes in the slices of cheese represent?

options.A: Weaknesses and vulnerabilities in safety defenses
options.B: The specific qualifications of the head nurse
options.C: Scheduled times for changing intravenous fluids
options.D: Patient complaints recorded during admission

explanation: Great job! Every safety barrier has tiny imperfections or gaps. When those gaps line up across different layers of defense, an error can slip through to the patient. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h2)

question: When MUST you use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: Immediately after removing clean, non-sterile examination gloves
options.B: Before taking a patient's routine blood pressure reading
options.C: When entering a patient room for a brief verbal assessment
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Spot on! If your hands have visible dirt, blood, or body fluids on them, alcohol rubs just won't cut it. You need good old soap and water to physically wash the mess away. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h2)

question: Which of these is classified as 'sharps' waste?

options.A: Hypodermic needles and scalpel blades
options.B: Disposable paper bed sheets
options.C: Cotton wool balls and surgical gauze
options.D: Plastic IV fluid bags and tubing

explanation: Easy and clear! Needles and blades have sharp edges that can puncture skin, so they need special handling. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of maintaining the cold chain in immunization programs?

options.A: To ensure vaccine potency and effectiveness

options.D: Surgical technicians

explanation: Social workers are experts in child protection, welfare placements, and finding safe homes or foster care. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T25#GNS225_U5_T25_h7)

question: What is the main point of using motivational interviewing during nutrition counseling?

options.A: Testing the patient on their knowledge of food biochemistry
options.B: Allowing the nurse to firmly dictate strict rules for weight loss
options.C: Speeding up the clinical consultation to save hospital time
options.D: Helping patients resolve their ambivalence about changing eating habits

explanation: Spot on. Motivational interviewing helps patients work through their mixed feelings so they can find their own inner drive to change. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h4)

question: What is the most important immediate nursing action after a fasting blood draw for a patient with diabetes?

options.A: Provide food and allow the patient to take held morning medications.
options.B: Send the patient home immediately without checking the puncture site.
options.C: Instruct the patient to continue fasting until the lab results return.
options.D: Encourage the patient to run on a treadmill to lower blood sugar.

explanation: Well done! Because the patient fasted and held their morning diabetes drugs, they need food and their routine medications right away to prevent their blood sugar from crashing. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h9)

question: A patient with severe anxiety is breathing very fast and deep (hyperventilating). What happens to their blood gas values?

options.A: Decreased carbon dioxide levels and increased pH
options.B: Increased bicarbonate retention by the lung tissue
options.C: Increased carbon dioxide levels and decreased pH
options.D: Decreased oxygen saturation in the arterial plasma

explanation: Fast breathing blows off too much $CO_2$. Less $CO_2$ means less acid in the blood, which causes the pH to rise (alkalosis). Makes sense, right? [learn more](GNS121_U2_T13#GNS121_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why don't petechiae and purpura turn white when you press your finger on them?

options.A: Blood has leaked entirely outside the blood vessels into the tissue
options.B: The underlying capillaries are permanently dilated from heat
options.C: The skin has become too thick from chronic scratching
options.D: There is an overproduction of clear serum inside the blister

explanation: Since the red blood cells have escaped right out into the skin tissue, pressing on top won't make the color go away. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T8#GNS213_U5_T8_h4)

question: A patient with a broken arm can walk around and is breathing fine. What triage color do they get?

options.A: Red
options.B: Yellow
options.C: Green
options.D: Black

explanation: Spot on! The 'walking wounded' with minor injuries get green tags and can wait safely while critical patients are treated. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T5#GNS315_U1_T5_h4)

question: A nurse finishes giving an intramuscular injection with a disposable syringe. Where should the nurse discard the needle?

options.A: Inside the general black municipal waste bin
options.B: Into a puncture-resistant yellow safety box
options.C: Inside a regular soft yellow plastic trash bag
options.D: On top of the medication preparation trolley

explanation: Sharps must go directly into a rigid safety box to prevent needle-stick injuries during transport. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h3)

question: A patient with severe nephrotic syndrome is most likely to report which initial pattern of swelling?

options.A: Severe swelling limited to the toes
options.B: Sudden swelling of only the right hand
options.C: Puffiness around the eyes upon waking up
options.D: Throbbing pain and swelling in the jaw

explanation: Periorbital edema is a classic early sign of fluid shifting into loose facial tissues overnight while the patient is lying flat. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h3)

question: A patient drinks two large mugs of strong craft beer every evening. Why might this be more alcohol than they realize?

options.A: Large mugs automatically convert alcohol into non-toxic carbohydrates
options.B: Beer loses its alcohol content completely when served in a mug
options.C: Fermented beverages do not register on standard liver enzyme tests
options.D: Craft beer usually contains a higher alcohol percentage and larger volume than a standard drink

explanation: A large mug holds way more liquid than a standard serving, and craft brews are often extra strong. One big mug can easily equal two or more standard drinks! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T013#GNS227_U4_T013_h1)

question: Why is patient education important before discharge on a modified diet?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will never need dental work again
options.B: It stops the patient from ever eating solid food
options.C: It helps family members prepare safe food textures at home
options.D: It replaces the need for follow-up doctor appointments

explanation: Educating patients and caregivers ensures they continue safe food preparation and know what to avoid after leaving the hospital. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h8)

question: What is the main difference between an in-text citation and a reference list?

options.A: An in-text citation goes at the very end, while the reference list goes at the beginning
options.B: An in-text citation uses numbers only, while the reference list uses only author names
options.C: An in-text citation is brief, while a reference list entry gives full publication details
options.D: An in-text citation is optional, while the reference list is mandatory

explanation: Exactly! The short in-text citation gives a quick peek, while the reference list gives the full picture of the source. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T7#GNS217_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of debriefing sessions for rescue personnel after an operation?

options.A: To punish team members who made minor mistakes during the rescue
options.B: To process emotional experiences and access mental health support
options.C: To calculate financial overtime pay and distribute hazard allowances
options.D: To conduct written examinations on disaster rescue theory

explanation: You've got this! Debriefings give rescue workers a safe space to talk through the heavy stress and trauma they witnessed on the job. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T3#GNS315_U5_T3_h8)

question: Which of these is a key part of psychological first aid provided by nurses after a disaster?

options.A: Prescribing heavy antipsychotic medication to all victims
options.B: Diagnosing long-term psychiatric disorders on the spot
options.C: Forcing survivors to recount traumatic details immediately
options.D: Offering a calm presence and practical assistance

explanation: You got it! Psychological first aid is all about being a calming, safe support and helping with basic needs—never forcing people to talk about trauma. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T4#GNS315_U1_T4_h8)

question: What would happen if the articular cartilage at the ends of your bones wore away completely?

options.A: The joint would produce too much fluid and swell instantly
options.B: The joint would lock permanently straight
options.C: Muscles would immediately lose their ability to contract
options.D: Bone surfaces would grind directly against each other, causing pain

explanation: Spot on! Cartilage is a smooth shock absorber. Without it, bare bones rub together, causing the pain and stiffness we see in arthritis. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is the main focus of manipulative and body-based therapies like massage?

options.A: The ingestion of raw botanical extracts
options.B: The manipulation of external spiritual energy fields
options.C: The physical structures and systems of the body
options.D: The psychological regulation of deep breathing

explanation: Well done! These therapies focus directly on working with the physical body parts, such as muscles and bones through massage or chiropractic care. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is the very first thing you need to do before drawing a scatter diagram?

options.A: Coloring the data points with bright markers
options.B: Gathering paired data for the variables
options.C: Calculating the final correlation coefficient
options.D: Drawing the title at the top of the page

explanation: You have to collect your matching pairs of data first before you can plot anything on a graph. Step by step! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T12#GNS217_U4_T12_h4)

question: How do your regular monthly payments (premiums) help you during a major medical emergency?

options.A: It stops the disease from spreading to family members
options.B: It guarantees immediate discharge from the hospital
options.C: It draws from a shared pool to pay for expensive treatments
options.D: It doubles the amount of medicine the doctor can prescribe

explanation: Spot on! Contributions from many people create a shared financial pool used to pay for individual medical care when emergencies happen. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why is 'replication' (repeating a study) so important in scientific nursing research?

options.A: It proves that the researcher is more important than the clinician
options.B: It helps verify whether original results were accurate and reliable
options.C: It eliminates the need for patient consent in clinical trials
options.D: It ensures that hospital policies never change again

explanation: When different researchers repeat a study and get the same results, we can trust that the findings are solid and dependable. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why is simply blaming a nurse after a clinical error usually ineffective?

options.A: It fails to address the underlying system flaws that caused the error
options.B: Nurses have legal immunity from all medication mistakes
options.C: Errors are always caused by faulty medical equipment alone
options.D: Administrators are not allowed to speak with staff nurses directly

explanation: Spot on! Errors are usually symptoms of deeper system traps. Punishing one person doesn't fix the root problem, meaning the same danger is still there for the next nurse. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a good strategy for helping a patient stick to a therapeutic diet long-term?

options.A: Involving family members in meal planning
options.B: Using herbs and spices to keep meals flavorful
options.C: Making gradual and sustainable food swaps
options.D: Making sudden, extreme food restrictions overnight without preparation

explanation: Going cold turkey on all your favorite foods overnight usually leads to burnout. Small, steady changes work best! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h8)

question: Which hormone is mostly responsible for preparing the lining of the womb for implantation?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Well done! Progesterone takes the lead in the second half of the cycle, making the womb lining thick and cozy for a potential pregnancy. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T2#GNS121_U6_T2_h3)

question: What is a major public health downside of relying solely on harsh criminal punishment for substance abuse?

options.A: It automatically cures physical dependence within forty-eight hours
options.B: It forces pharmaceutical companies to stop manufacturing all antibiotics
options.C: It drives vulnerable drug users underground and prevents them from seeking medical help
options.D: It eliminates every single illegal drug farm in the entire world

explanation: When people fear police arrest and prison, they tend to stay away from hospitals during overdoses or medical crises, which puts lives at risk. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which practice should a nurse avoid when writing an incident report after a client falls off the bed?

options.A: Writing speculative comments and blaming other staff members in the report
options.B: Notifying the attending physician about the fall immediately
options.C: Recording objective facts about how the client was found
options.D: Documenting the exact time and physical condition of the client

explanation: Incident reports should contain only objective facts without personal opinions, emotional language, or assigning blame. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h8)

question: What was the big shift in thinking brought by the Ottawa Charter?

options.A: Transferring all health responsibilities from governments to private individuals
options.B: Mandating that every village must build a modern tertiary hospital
options.C: Focusing exclusively on pharmaceutical distribution in developing nations
options.D: Shifting focus away from just treating sickness toward social and environmental living conditions

explanation: You've got this! The Charter expanded our understanding of health beyond just hospitals and doctors to include living conditions, policies, and community environments. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which assessment finding is a reliable indicator of poor peripheral tissue perfusion?

options.A: Warm and pink extremities
options.B: Cool, pale, or bluish skin
options.C: Rapid and clear speech
options.D: Bounding radial pulse strength

explanation: Cold, pale, or cyanotic skin often means blood flow to the skin and outer tissues is reduced. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h7)

question: Why is family planning counseling a must before a patient is discharged from PAC?

options.A: It helps prevent repeat unintended pregnancies and repeat abortions
options.B: It satisfies legal requirements for hospital record keeping
options.C: It determines the exact gestational age of the previous pregnancy
options.D: It completely eliminates the risk of postpartum depression

explanation: You'll learn in practice that fertility can return very quickly after an abortion. Giving contraceptive counseling right away empowers your patient to space or prevent future pregnancies safely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h1)

question: When two rescuers are doing CPR on a child, what is the compression-to-ventilation ratio?

options.A: 5 compressions to 1 breath
options.B: 30 compressions to 2 breaths
options.C: 100 compressions to 5 breaths
options.D: 15 compressions to 2 breaths

explanation: When you have two people working together on a pediatric patient, you use a 15:2 ratio to get more rescue breaths into the child. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to know the basic anatomy of these internal organs?

options.A: To properly assess pelvic pain and provide education
options.B: To diagnose complex endocrine disorders independently
options.C: To surgically repair damaged uterine tissue
options.D: To perform routine blood pressure checks

explanation: Understanding where organs sit helps nurses interpret patient symptoms and teach them about reproductive health. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is a documented benefit of open parent-child communication regarding sexual health?

options.A: Delayed sexual debut and increased contraceptive use
options.B: Total elimination of teenage peer pressure
options.C: Immediate loss of interest in romantic relationships
options.D: Guaranteed immunity from all reproductive infections

explanation: When families discuss sexual health openly and calmly, teenagers tend to make safer choices and delay risky behaviors. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h4)

question: Why do hospitals prefer a centralized TSSU instead of letting individual wards clean their own surgical tools?

options.A: It reduces the cost of purchasing brand new instruments
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for chemical disinfectants
options.C: It allows nurses to spend more time at the patient bedside
options.D: It ensures consistent and strict quality control standards

explanation: Great thinking! When trained specialists handle sterilization in one central place, you can trust that every single instrument goes through the exact same high safety checks every time. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h1)

question: A nurse notices that two different injectable drugs have very similar label designs and are stored right next to each other. What is the best immediate risk reduction action?

options.A: Report the labeling issue to pharmacy and management and separate the drugs
options.B: Wait until a medication error actually happens before telling anyone
options.C: Tell the patients not to accept any injections from other staff
options.D: Hide one of the drugs in a private pocket so nobody else uses it

explanation: Spotted look-alike hazards should be immediately separated and reported to prevent a future mix-up. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h6)

question: Why must public health measures continue even if a disease is wiped out in Nigeria?

options.A: Local health workers lose their medical licenses after an outbreak
options.B: The pathogen can still be imported from other regions where it exists
options.C: Patients will develop allergies if vaccination programs stop
options.D: Eliminated diseases always mutate into completely different organisms

explanation: As long as the germ is active in other parts of the world, travelers or animals can easily bring it back across borders. Stay alert! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is another common name for psychiatric parole in mental health care?

options.A: Forced institutionalization
options.B: Conditional release
options.C: Absolute discharge
options.D: Criminal extradition

explanation: Spot on! Psychiatric parole is often called conditional release because patients leave the hospital to continue their recovery under specific medical and legal conditions. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T8#GNS314_U5_T8_h1)

question: Which specific bone cells are responsible for breaking down or resorbing bone tissue?

options.A: Osteons
options.B: Osteoblasts
options.C: Osteocytes
options.D: Osteoclasts

explanation: Remember: Osteoclasts 'c'rve or 'c'ut bone down! They break down old bone tissue to help with remodeling and keep blood calcium levels balanced. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T1#GNS222_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which agricultural expense involves paying planting crews and harvesting staff?

options.A: Seed patents
options.B: Fertilizer tariffs
options.C: Labor costs
options.D: Environmental subsidies

explanation: Labor encompasses the wages paid to workers who physically plant, manage, and harvest crops. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a thorough initial prenatal booking visit?

options.A: To administer the final dose of the tetanus vaccine
options.B: To perform an emergency delivery for safety
options.C: To establish a complete baseline health and obstetric history
options.D: To finalize the birth certificate before delivery

explanation: Think of the booking visit as your complete roadmap. Gathering all her past and current health details helps you guide her safely through the rest of the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h3)

question: Why are human reservoirs who show no symptoms harder to manage during an outbreak than sick patients?

options.A: They refuse to take any form of laboratory testing
options.B: Their immune systems are naturally immune to all treatments
options.C: The germs they carry are invisible to standard microscopes
options.D: They continue normal daily activities and spread germs unknowingly

explanation: Because healthy carriers do not feel sick, they do not isolate themselves, allowing them to pass pathogens to many people during routine interactions. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h2)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with a cough lasting four weeks, drenching night sweats, and sudden weight loss. What should you suspect first?

options.A: Acute tension headache
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Simple seasonal allergy
options.D: Pulmonary tuberculosis

explanation: A long-standing cough, night sweats, and dropping weight without trying form the classic triad for active pulmonary TB. Great clinical spotting! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the main difference between disinfection and antisepsis?

options.A: Disinfection targets inanimate surfaces, while antisepsis is applied to living tissue
options.B: Disinfection kills bacterial spores, while antisepsis only removes visible dirt
options.C: Disinfection requires heat, while antisepsis relies entirely on cold water washing
options.D: Disinfection is used on living skin, while antisepsis is used on inanimate tables

explanation: It's all about where it goes! Antiseptics are safe for human skin, while disinfectants are meant for hard surfaces like tables and bed rails. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h3)

question: Why is relying solely on clinical tradition dangerous in modern healthcare?

options.A: Patients always reject care based on historical habits
options.B: Traditions are often outdated and unsupported by current evidence
options.C: Traditions cost too much money to maintain in hospitals
options.D: Physicians refuse to follow traditional nursing methods

explanation: Habits passed down through generations of staff may be ineffective or even harmful compared to modern tested methods. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h1)

question: What can happen if educators overlook cultural differences in communication?

options.A: They will automatically improve student test scores in pharmacology
options.B: They remove all language barriers from clinical wards
options.C: They ensure all students learn at the exact same speed
options.D: They might misinterpret a student's respectful quietness as laziness

explanation: In some cultures, staying completely quiet around elders or teachers is a sign of deep respect. Instructors need to understand this so they don't misjudge a student. [learn more](GST321_U8_T9#GST321_U8_T9_h5)

question: Which ethical principle refers to the nurse's core duty to do no harm to patients?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Justice
options.C: Non-maleficence
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Great nursing foundation here! 'Non-maleficence' literally means avoiding any physical, emotional, or psychological harm to the patients in your care. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h6)

question: Why is proper nutrition considered a core element of Primary Health Care?

options.A: Nutrition is only important for professional athletes
options.B: Good nutrition strengthens immunity and prevents infectious diseases
options.C: Eating expensive foreign food cures chronic illnesses
options.D: Food supply is managed strictly by the federal military

explanation: Well-nourished bodies fight off infections much more effectively, reducing the burden of disease in the community. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h3)

question: What major mistake should you avoid when writing the results section?

options.A: Using tables and charts to summarize numerical findings
options.B: Including personal interpretations and opinions about the data
options.C: Reporting findings that go against the original hypothesis
options.D: Stating the exact statistical values found in the study

explanation: Keep the results section strictly factual! Save your opinions and deep meanings for the discussion chapter. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h6)

question: What life-threatening emergency happens when fluid overload backs up all the way into the lungs?

options.A: Pleural mesothelioma
options.B: Chronic bronchial asthma
options.C: Spontaneous pneumothorax
options.D: Acute pulmonary edema

explanation: When the kidneys can't clear fluid, it backs up into the air sacs (alveoli) of the lungs, causing acute pulmonary edema and severe breathing distress. You're mastering critical care concepts! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h8)

question: Why might a muscular athlete be flagged as overweight when using BMI alone?

options.A: Bone density decreases in athletes, throwing off the calculation
options.B: The standard BMI formula only applies to sedentary individuals
options.C: Athletes typically retain excess water weight during training seasons
options.D: Muscle tissue is much denser than fat tissue, increasing total body weight

explanation: Exactly right! Muscle weighs more per volume than fat, so heavy muscle mass can push up a person's BMI even if they have very little body fat. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T10#GNS121_U1_T10_h4)

question: What are the three main tiers of the Nigerian health system?

options.A: Local, state, and federal hospitals
options.B: Community, general, and teaching units
options.C: Primary, secondary, and tertiary care
options.D: Private, public, and missionary clinics

explanation: Spot on! Nigeria's health system is broken into three simple levels (primary, secondary, and tertiary) to make sure healthcare reaches everyone from local villages to big cities. [learn more](GST322_U5_T4#GST322_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which major health issue deeply affects young people worldwide?

options.A: Unplanned pregnancies and sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Advanced age-related joint degeneration
options.C: Chronic occupational lung diseases
options.D: Severe childhood developmental delays

explanation: Correct! Adolescents face serious reproductive health challenges, which makes targeted education and friendly services so important. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T17#GNS312_U3_T17_h2)

question: A community nurse is advising Nigerian mothers on affordable toddler meals. Which approach works best?

options.A: Tell mothers to avoid local vegetables because they lack minerals
options.B: Encourage combining local staples like beans and grains to make balanced meals
options.C: Insist that only imported tinned foods provide enough vitamins for growth
options.D: Advise mothers to feed the child only once a day with a large heavy meal

explanation: Brilliant! Using affordable local foods like beans and maize is sustainable, cost-effective, and keeps our little ones well-nourished. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h7)

question: How are descriptive statistics different from inferential statistics?

options.A: Descriptive statistics are only used in qualitative studies, while inferential ones are for charts.
options.B: Descriptive statistics summarize data, while inferential statistics test hypotheses and make generalizations.
options.C: Descriptive statistics test if results happened by chance, while inferential statistics summarize data.
options.D: Descriptive statistics require large populations, while inferential statistics use only single patients.

explanation: Think of descriptive stats as painting a picture of what your current data looks like, while inferential stats help you look beyond your data to make bigger conclusions. Great job! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T3#GNS217_U4_T3_h1)

question: Under the Abuja Declaration, what percentage of their annual budget should African governments put toward health?

options.A: Five percent of private sector corporate profits
options.B: Ten percent of all international donor funds received
options.C: Exactly 50 percent of the total Gross Domestic Product
options.D: At least 15 percent of the annual national budget

explanation: The famous Abuja Declaration set a benchmark of at least 15% for national health budgets. Great to keep in mind for your exams! [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h3)

question: What happens when many nurses leave public hospitals for private clinics because of better pay?

options.A: Immediate elimination of all health disparities
options.B: Brain drain in the public health sector
options.C: Mandatory free nursing education nationwide
options.D: Excessive surplus of staff in public teaching hospitals

explanation: When skilled health workers migrate to better-paying sectors en masse, public hospitals are left short-staffed, which is a big challenge known as brain drain. [learn more](GST322_U5_T3#GST322_U5_T3_h8)

question: A patient with acute diarrhoea has sore, red skin around their bottom. What is the best immediate nursing step?

options.A: Instruct the patient to avoid washing the area until stools stop
options.B: Gently clean the area, pat dry, and apply a barrier cream
options.C: Place a tight-fitting dressing over the skin to block moisture
options.D: Apply an alcohol-based wipe to disinfect the raw skin thoroughly

explanation: Frequent watery stools are very irritating to the skin. Keeping the area clean, dry, and protected with a good barrier cream is a nursing lifesaver for comfort and skin integrity. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which factor is primarily responsible for urge faecal incontinence?

options.A: Excessive production of stomach acid
options.B: Weakened sphincters unable to hold back a strong bowel urge
options.C: Permanent blockage of the upper gastrointestinal tract
options.D: Complete absence of the large intestine

explanation: In urge incontinence, the patient perceives the need to defecate, but weak muscles cannot keep the stool contained long enough to reach a toilet. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why might a nurse researcher choose an observational checklist instead of a patient questionnaire?

options.A: Patients prefer being watched over writing answers
options.B: What people say they do can differ from their actual actions
options.C: Observational checklists are much cheaper to print
options.D: Questionnaires cannot be used in a hospital setting

explanation: Direct observation captures real behavior, avoiding the bias or forgetfulness that comes with self-reporting. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h5)

question: What is a common resource barrier faced by nurses trying to maintain quality care in Nigeria?

options.A: An excess of trained nurses with no patients to care for
options.B: Too much free time leading to staff boredom
options.C: Having too many modern computers on every ward
options.D: Shortages of basic consumables like gloves and disinfectants

explanation: It's a tough reality, but lacking basic tools like gloves and clean water makes it super hard to maintain standard infection control. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h6)

question: How long must close contacts of an Ebola patient be watched for signs of illness?

options.A: 5 days
options.B: 3 months
options.C: 48 hours
options.D: 21 days

explanation: Spot on! Since the incubation period is up to 21 days, we keep track of contacts for that full period to catch any early signs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h7)

question: What is the main goal of evaluating population health programs?

options.A: To write promotional brochures for the local government ministry
options.B: To find staff members to blame when a project runs out of money
options.C: To increase the cost of medical services for community residents
options.D: To determine whether the health interventions actually achieved their intended goals

explanation: Evaluation measures the real-world impact of health programs so nurses know what is working and what needs improvement. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which research question is best suited for a quantitative approach?

options.A: What are the emotional challenges of being a first-time ward manager?
options.B: How do patients describe their spiritual journey in palliative care?
options.C: What does it feel like to live with chronic kidney failure?
options.D: Does a 10mg dose of medication lower blood pressure faster than a 5mg dose?

explanation: Because we are measuring dosage amounts and blood pressure numbers, we need a numerical, quantitative study design. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h5)

question: What should the nurse instruct the patient to do immediately before actuating a metered-dose inhaler?

options.A: Inhale as fast as possible through the nose
options.B: Hyperventilate for thirty seconds
options.C: Exhale completely to empty the lungs
