question: How is a research hypothesis different from a research question?

options.A: A hypothesis is always written in the form of a question
options.B: A research question contains independent variables only
options.C: A hypothesis is a declarative statement of predicted outcome
options.D: A research question can never be tested statistically

explanation: Questions ask what might happen, but hypotheses make a bold, clear statement of what you predict the results will be. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T10#GNS217_U3_T10_h6)

question: Besides physical safety, what else helps create a healing ward environment?

options.A: Playing loud music to keep patients awake during the day
options.B: Keeping the lights at maximum brightness twenty-four hours a day
options.C: Allowing visitors to stay without any time limits
options.D: Reducing noise and addressing patient grievances promptly

explanation: You've got this! Healing isn't just physical—lowering stress by keeping noise down and listening to patient complaints makes a huge difference. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h6)

question: Why does a pregnant woman's body become more sensitive to carbon dioxide?

options.A: To clear waste products and match higher oxygen demands
options.B: To prevent the lungs from collapsing during rest
options.C: To prepare the muscle tissue for postpartum bleeding
options.D: To slow down the heart rate and conserve energy

explanation: Being sensitive to CO2 forces mum to breathe a bit more actively, sweeping away waste for both herself and the growing foetus. Brilliant effort! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T3#GNS121_U7_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a normal, healthy personality pattern?

options.A: Rigid and inflexible responses to everyday life stress
options.B: Ability to form deep and meaningful relationships with others
options.C: Realistic and honest perception of one's own self
options.D: Emotional flexibility when handling unexpected challenges

explanation: Rigid responses point toward a maladaptive pattern, whereas healthy personalities are flexible and adaptable. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T8#GNS314_U1_T8_h4)

question: A patient uses prayer and talks daily with a peer support group to handle chronic pain. What coping strategy is this?

options.A: Maladaptive avoidance
options.B: Problem-focused coping
options.C: Emotion-focused coping
options.D: Aggressive confrontation

explanation: Great job! Spiritual practices and support groups help manage the emotional weight of stress, even when the physical pain itself doesn't vanish. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T14#GNS225_U5_T14_h6)

question: In which situation would you expect a patient to be placed on a fluid diet?

options.A: During long-term rehabilitation for a chronic leg fracture
options.B: Immediately following abdominal surgery before bowel sounds return
options.C: As a permanent meal plan for an active adolescent
options.D: To treat long-term iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Right after surgery, the gut is sleeping! Fluids are gentle and safe until the bowel wakes back up. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T001#GNS227_U6_T001_h2)

question: Why is the chain of infection like a link fence? What happens if you break just one link?

options.A: Pathogens require all six links to survive inside a reservoir
options.B: Breaking any single link stops the infection from spreading
options.C: The immune system only attacks pathogens when all links are full
options.D: Microorganisms multiply faster when every link is connected

explanation: You've got it! Think of infection control as stopping a chain reaction. If you wash your hands or clean a surface, you break the chain of transmission and stop the disease in its tracks. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which of these waste items goes into a rigid, puncture-resistant container?

options.A: Soiled paper hand towels and napkins
options.B: Empty plastic intravenous fluid bags
options.C: Used needles and surgical blades
options.D: Clean cotton balls and packaging paper

explanation: Correct! Sharp items like blades and needles need hard, puncture-proof walls so they don't poke through and injure nurses or waste handlers. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h6)

question: What is the go-to medication used to stop and prevent seizures in eclampsia?

options.A: Oxytocin infusion
options.B: Diazepam injection
options.C: Magnesium sulfate
options.D: Sodium bicarbonate

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is our absolute best friend in emergency obstetrics for keeping eclamptic seizures at bay and protecting the mother. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h6)

question: What is the main goal of doing a Spontaneous Breathing Trial (SBT)?

options.A: To measure the exact lung compliance and resistance parameters
options.B: To evaluate if a patient can tolerate breathing without ventilator support
options.C: To allow the patient to recover from heavy sedative medications
options.D: To clear thick mucus plugs from the lower airways before extubation

explanation: An SBT is like a test drive! We lower the machine's help to see if the patient's lungs and muscles are strong enough to handle breathing all on their own. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T18#GNS213_U2_T18_h7)

question: Which government program became the main payer for long-term nursing home care after 1965?

options.A: Medicare
options.B: The Hill-Burton fund
options.C: Social Security
options.D: Medicaid

explanation: Medicaid was built to support low-income individuals, and over time it grew to become the primary financial backbone paying for long-term stays in nursing facilities. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which group of vegetables is famous for helping your liver clear out toxins?

options.A: Cruciferous vegetables
options.B: Root and tuber vegetables
options.C: Fruiting vegetables
options.D: Leafy green vegetables

explanation: Spot on! Vegetables like cabbage and broccoli belong to the cruciferous family and contain special compounds that give your liver a helping hand. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T009#GNS227_U4_T009_h2)

question: When healthcare workers rely on 'tradition,' what is their main mindset?

options.A: Only randomized controlled trials can guide nursing care
options.B: We do it this way because we have always done it this way
options.C: Personal gut feelings are more reliable than textbooks
options.D: Every patient requires a completely unique laboratory workup

explanation: Tradition leans heavily on past habits and routines rather than checking if newer, better methods are available. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which payment model requires a patient to pay the full cost right at the moment of receiving treatment?

options.A: National health insurance
options.B: Donor funding grants
options.C: Cooperative risk pools
options.D: User fees

explanation: User fees are paid straight out of pocket by the patient right at the point of service delivery. It's a very common system, though tough on families during emergencies! [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which age group is most commonly affected by febrile seizures?

options.A: Adolescence to early adulthood
options.B: Advanced old age
options.C: Birth to three months
options.D: Six months to five years

explanation: Febrile seizures typically occur in young children whose developing nervous systems react strongly to rapid temperature increases. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h5)

question: On the AVPU neurological scale, what does the letter 'V' stand for?

options.A: Voice
options.B: Ventilation
options.C: Vomiting
options.D: Vascular

explanation: Remember AVPU: Alert, Voice-responsive, Pain-responsive, and Unresponsive. It's a quick and handy way to check mental status! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h2)

question: How long must symptoms of ODD be present to meet standard diagnostic criteria?

options.A: More than five years
options.B: At least two weeks
options.C: At least six months
options.D: Exactly one month

explanation: Diagnostic manuals require a duration of at least six months of persistent irritable and defiant behavior for an ODD diagnosis. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T1#GNS314_U2_T1_h2)

question: How would you describe a direct cost in patient care?

options.A: An unexpected emergency expense covered by insurance
options.B: The overall electricity bill for the entire hospital building
options.C: An expense easily traced to a specific patient or unit
options.D: A hidden fee charged by hospital administrators

explanation: Direct costs point straight to one specific place or person—like the exact medication or supplies given to a particular patient. Simple and clear! [learn more](GST322_U2_T2#GST322_U2_T2_h2)

question: What three main disciplines are combined in nursing informatics?

options.A: Biology, pharmacology, and hospital administration
options.B: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.C: Public health, statistics, and clinical psychology
options.D: Medicine, engineering, and health economics

explanation: Nursing informatics is defined by the integration of nursing science with computer and information sciences to manage healthcare data. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why do nursing students need to learn about different sources of knowledge?

options.A: To eliminate the need for clinical experience entirely
options.B: To memorize every historical medical text ever written
options.C: To understand why clinical guidelines change and why evidence matters
options.D: To learn how to diagnose patients without a doctor

explanation: Knowing where knowledge comes from helps you see why nursing care changes for the better as new evidence comes to light. You've got this! [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which type of cervical traction involves putting metal pins directly into the skull bone?

options.A: Manual traction
options.B: Halter traction
options.C: Skin traction
options.D: Halo traction

explanation: Great job! Skeletal traction (like a halo device) uses metal pins right in the bone so it can handle much stronger pulling forces. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T12#GNS221_U1_T12_h2)

question: Why should a nurse manager look for the root cause before penalizing an error?

options.A: Many errors are caused by broken workflows rather than careless staff
options.B: Punishing staff members is illegal in all healthcare facilities
options.C: Hospital labor unions forbid managers from talking to individual nurses
options.D: Root cause analysis is only required for surgical complications

explanation: If a faulty system or bad equipment caused the mistake, punishing the nurse won't stop it from happening again to someone else. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h6)

question: A healthy 50-year-old woman asks why she needs a routine mammogram when she feels fine. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Routine screening is legally required for all women over the age of forty in this country.
options.B: Screening tests catch cancer early before symptoms develop, which makes treatment more successful.
options.C: These tests are designed to prevent normal cells from ever mutating into cancerous growths.
options.D: Mammograms are only performed after a physician feels a distinct lump during a physical exam.

explanation: Screening is all about catching things early before they turn into bigger problems. Early detection makes treatment much easier! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why is it important for nursing students to understand how healthcare is funded?

options.A: Nurses are directly responsible for collecting hospital revenue
options.B: It explains why some facilities lack basic supplies and equipment
options.C: It is required for writing national health policies
options.D: It determines the specific salary scale for health workers

explanation: You've got this! Knowing where hospital money comes from helps you make sense of the real-world shortages and everyday challenges you will see during clinical postings. [learn more](GST322_U5_T4#GST322_U5_T4_h1)

question: What triggers the release of the hormone cholecystokinin (CCK) during digestion?

options.A: The drop in pH inside the stomach lumen
options.B: The presence of fats and proteins in the duodenum
options.C: The smell of food before it enters the mouth
options.D: The arrival of water in the large intestine

explanation: When fats and proteins hit the first part of your small intestine (duodenum), CCK gets released. It tells the gallbladder to squeeze out bile and the pancreas to release its enzymes! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T011#GNS227_U1_T011_h8)

question: Why do care teams use psychiatric parole instead of keeping a stable patient locked away long-term?

options.A: It allows the legal system to permanently forget about the patient's case.
options.B: It supports recovery in a less restrictive setting while keeping everyone safe.
options.C: It completely removes the need for any ongoing medical supervision.
options.D: It saves money by stopping all prescription medication costs.

explanation: You got it! Conditional release finds that sweet spot between keeping the community safe and allowing the patient to heal in a normal environment. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T8#GNS314_U5_T8_h1)

question: A baby is born with an omphalocele (abdominal organs outside the belly). What is your very first action in the delivery room?

options.A: Give the infant a warm bath to clean them up
options.B: Feed the baby immediately to boost sugar
options.C: Cover the organs with a warm, sterile saline-soaked wrap
options.D: Gently push the organs back inside the tummy

explanation: Protect those exposed organs right away! A warm, moist wrap keeps them safe from infection, injury, and drying out until surgery can happen. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a good nursing action when managing an outbreak using incubation data?

options.A: Prescribing broad-spectrum antibiotics to every community resident
options.B: Calculating the probable exposure date for sick patients
options.C: Stocking adequate testing supplies for anticipated surges
options.D: Educating exposed contacts on why they need to monitor symptoms

explanation: Spot on! Giving out unnecessary antibiotics causes drug resistance. Nurses focus on tracking, educating, and supporting the community instead. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T9#GNS313_U1_T9_h6)

question: What does 'bivariate data' mean when working on a nursing research project?

options.A: Measurements are taken twice on the same patient
options.B: Two different variables are collected from each subject
options.C: Two researchers analyze the same set of numbers
options.D: Data is gathered from two separate hospitals at once

explanation: Bivariate just means two pieces of information (like a patient's age and their blood pressure) are gathered from each person. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T12#GNS217_U4_T12_h1)

question: A patient is nearly ready for independent life and only needs short-term guidance on budgeting and job hunting. Which facility fits best?

options.A: Transitional living facility
options.B: Long-term nursing home
options.C: Maximum security asylum
options.D: Acute psychiatric ward

explanation: You nailed it! Transitional facilities are short-term setups designed to help patients brush up on practical skills like managing money and finding jobs before they head out on their own. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h3)

question: Why are transdermal patches unique compared to standard topical creams?

options.C: They are completely water-soluble and wash off easily with light sweat

question: Why do policymakers need data gathered from a community diagnosis?

options.A: To prove that no diseases exist in rural areas
options.B: To increase the workload of community health nurses
options.C: To create policies based on actual local facts rather than guesses
options.D: To find reasons to close down poorly performing village clinics

explanation: Evidence-based planning ensures that health policies directly address proven local realities rather than assumptions. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why should a nurse always recommend locally available and affordable foods when giving diet advice?

options.A: It ensures the client can maintain the diet long-term
options.B: It guarantees that the food contains zero calories
options.C: It replaces the need for any professional medical care
options.D: It prevents the client from ever needing clean water

question: What is the main danger of giving a medication that another nurse prepared?

options.A: Patients prefer when the same nurse handles their entire admission

options.C: You cannot verify the accuracy of the calculation or sterility

question: What is the main limitation of a chemical indicator strip placed inside an instrument tray?

options.A: It can only be read using an ultraviolet microscope

options.C: It only measures the external room temperature of the storage area
options.D: It shows that conditions for sterilization occurred, but not that spores are dead

explanation: Chemical strips change color when exposed to heat or steam, which proves the machine got hot enough. However, they don't test actual germ survival like biological tests do. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which facility represents the primary level of mental health care in Nigeria?

options.A: University teaching hospitals
options.B: Local government health clinics and posts

question: As a fresh graduate, what is the very first official step you must take toward getting your license?

options.A: Payment of lifetime indemnity insurance fees to the federal treasury

options.C: Submission of architectural drawings of a proposed private clinic
options.D: Educational verification of certificates from an accredited school

question: Why do droplet precautions require masks only when close to the patient?

options.A: Droplet germs disappear completely after three minutes

options.C: Masks stop working if you walk past three feet
options.D: Germs in droplets cannot survive inside a hospital

question: Why is just handing out a new safety checklist usually not enough to change hospital practice?

options.A: Habits require ongoing reinforcement and audit to stick
options.B: Checklists are illegal in most healthcare settings
options.C: Doctors refuse to let nurses use checklists
options.D: Paper checklists take too much time to complete

explanation: Just giving out a new tool won't change daily habits unless there is proper follow-up, training, and regular performance checks. [learn more](GST319_U6_T6#GST319_U6_T6_h7)

question: What is the normal age range for the closure of the larger anterior fontanelle?

options.A: 1 to 3 months
options.B: 6 to 8 weeks

options.D: 24 to 36 months

question: What action should a nurse take immediately before leaving a computer workstation on the ward?

options.A: Lock or log out of the workstation to prevent unauthorized access
options.B: Minimize the patient charts without locking the screen
options.C: Turn off the main electrical power switch in the room
options.D: Leave the screen open for the next shift nurse

explanation: Locking unattended screens prevents unauthorized people from viewing confidential patient health records. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h6)

question: What happens to a student's brain when the classroom environment feels unsafe or hostile?

options.A: You suddenly feel super creative and relaxed
options.B: You focus on survival and anxiety rather than solving problems
options.C: You instantly become a great class leader
options.D: You find it twice as easy to memorize drugs

explanation: When you feel threatened or scared of being ridiculed, fear takes over, making it really hard to concentrate on learning new clinical skills. [learn more](GST321_U8_T3#GST321_U8_T3_h3)

question: A patient asks why they must finish all their antibiotics even after feeling better. What is the best response?

options.A: Stopping early can let stronger, resistant bacteria survive and cause a worse infection
options.B: Pharmacies will not accept returned medication bottles once opened
options.C: The remaining pills are needed to improve your daily sleep cycle
options.D: Unfinished pills will permanently alter your blood type if thrown away

explanation: Spot on! Stopping early leaves the toughest germs alive to breed resistance. Patient education here stops superbugs from spreading! [learn more](GST114_U5_T3#GST114_U5_T3_h8)

question: Which of these is a natural, drug-free way to help a mum cope with labour pain?

options.A: Epidural anesthesia block
options.B: Intravenous opioid administration
options.C: Continuous back rubs and hydrotherapy
options.D: General surgical anesthesia

explanation: Massages, warm water (hydrotherapy), and breathing exercises work wonders for natural pain relief without medications. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T002#GNS226_U3_T002_h7)

question: If a patient has a large left-sided tension pneumothorax, which way is the trachea likely to shift?

options.A: Tracheal deviation toward the left side
options.B: Downward displacement of the liver
options.C: Tracheal deviation toward the right side
options.D: No movement of the mediastinal structures

question: What do socio-economic determinants of health primarily include?

options.A: The daily weather and temperature
options.B: Genetic mutations inherited from parents
options.C: Income, employment, and education levels
options.D: Blood pressure and cholesterol levels

explanation: Socio-economic factors relate to social and economic standing, such as how much money people make, their jobs, and their level of education. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the most common hormonal condition behind oligomenorrhoea in young women?

options.A: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.B: Addison's disease
options.C: Cushing's disease
options.D: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

question: What do we mean by the term 'opportunity cost' in health economics?

options.A: The profit a pharmaceutical company makes on a new vaccine
options.B: The value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made
options.C: The total amount of money a hospital spends on patient medications
options.D: The discount given to patients who pay for medical care in cash

explanation: Think of opportunity cost as what you sacrifice. When you choose to spend your last Naira on transport instead of snacks, the snack is your opportunity cost! [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is a key feature of positive discipline?

options.A: Personal accountability and mutual respect
options.B: Heavy financial fines for minor errors
options.C: Strict reliance on fear and threats
options.D: Immediate suspension without investigation

explanation: Positive discipline encourages workers to take responsibility for their actions through cooperation. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h2)

question: What is the main legal fear many healthcare workers have about apologizing?

options.A: That hospital management will cut their monthly housing allowances
options.B: That the nursing council will revoke their license within twenty-four hours
options.C: That patients will demand free medication for the rest of their lives
options.D: That saying sorry will be used as an immediate admission of legal liability

explanation: Many nurses worry that saying 'I'm sorry' will be used in court as a direct confession that they were negligent. [learn more](GST319_U6_T3#GST319_U6_T3_h5)

question: Which pattern of knowing represents the science of nursing derived from research?

options.A: Empirical knowing
options.B: Ethical knowing
options.C: Aesthetic knowing
options.D: Personal knowing

explanation: Empirical knowing is your go-to science foundation—it relies on objective, observable data and actual research findings. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the primary definition of maternal morbidity in nursing practice?

options.A: Any health condition resulting from or worsened by pregnancy and childbirth
options.B: The permanent inability to conceive after experiencing a miscarriage
options.C: Any psychological stress experienced immediately after delivering a baby
options.D: The total number of maternal deaths recorded in a specific community

explanation: Maternal morbidity covers any physical or mental condition that affects a woman because of pregnancy, childbirth, or the postpartum period, short of death itself. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h1)

question: What is the best imaging test to check for liver hydatid cysts?

options.A: Electrocardiography
options.B: X-ray fluoroscopy
options.C: Ultrasound
options.D: Positron emission tomography

explanation: Ultrasound is safe and brilliant at spotting fluid-filled cysts hiding inside the liver. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T25#GNS313_U2_T25_h6)

question: Why are non-human reservoirs so important in the spread of diseases?

options.A: They purify local water sources so that waterborne parasites cannot infect people
options.B: They manufacture natural antibodies that help human populations fight off severe infections
options.C: They serve as temporary quarantine stations for individuals exposed to outbreaks
options.D: They provide a safe place for the infectious agent to survive and multiply over time

explanation: Spot on! Reservoirs act like safe breeding grounds for germs, making sure the disease cycle keeps going if we don't intervene. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is infection control often trickier in a patient's home compared to a hospital ward?

options.A: Standard precautions are legally prohibited in private residences
options.B: The environment is dynamic and outside direct professional control
options.C: Clients in homes always carry more dangerous bacteria
options.D: Hospitals lack the sanitation resources found in households

question: What makes corporate negligence different from vicarious liability?

options.A: Corporate negligence protects the hospital from all lawsuits.

options.C: Corporate negligence only applies to private clinics, not public hospitals.
options.D: Vicarious liability covers faulty equipment while corporate covers staff.

explanation: While vicarious liability is about staff mistakes, corporate negligence happens when the hospital itself messes up—like hiring unqualified workers or failing to fix broken equipment. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h6)

question: What is the main advantage of an EHR over an EMR?

options.A: An EHR is cheaper to install and requires no electricity or computer network
options.B: An EHR is designed to share patient data across multiple different healthcare organizations
options.C: An EHR requires physical paper backup files for every single digital entry
options.D: An EHR can only be accessed by medical doctors and never by nursing staff

explanation: The key benefit of an EHR is interoperability, meaning information flows seamlessly across different hospitals, clinics, and specialists. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h2)

question: You pick up a sterile tray and notice the outer wrap is damp. What should you do?

options.C: Reject the tray and obtain a new one because moisture causes contamination
options.D: Place the pack back into the warming cabinet until the moisture evaporates

question: Which of these is a major challenge to quality assurance in many Nigerian healthcare settings?

options.A: Shortages of nursing personnel and equipment
options.B: Excessive funding for nursing research programs
options.C: Too many nurses working in rural health centers
options.D: An overabundance of advanced medical technology

explanation: Unfortunately, staff shortages and a lack of basic tools are very real hurdles we face when trying to maintain high care standards in many of our hospitals. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which management system do hospitals use during emergencies to keep a clear chain of command?

options.B: The Nursing Process Evaluation Model
options.C: The Incident Command System (ICS)
options.D: The Primary Health Care Algorithm

explanation: In an emergency, everyone needs to know who is in charge. The ICS provides a clear, organized leadership structure so rescue efforts run smoothly. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which of these patients is most at risk of catching a hospital infection?

options.A: A middle-aged nurse working full-time in the surgical ward
options.B: A healthy outpatient visiting the clinic for a routine checkup
options.C: A young adult recovering from a simple sprained ankle
options.D: An elderly patient receiving chemotherapy and using a urinary catheter

explanation: Exactly. Between age, chemotherapy lowering their immunity, and a catheter creating an easy entry path, this patient's defenses are stretched thin. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary law guiding nursing practice and training in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Public Service General Orders
options.B: Nigerian Medical and Dental Practitioners Act
options.C: National Health Insurance Authority Act
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Registration Act

explanation: This is the core law that established the nursing council and sets the legal boundaries for our practice in Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h5)

question: During a surgical hand scrub, which way should the rinse water always flow?

options.A: From elbows down toward the fingertips
options.B: Upward toward the shoulders and neck
options.C: Straight off the hands without dripping
options.D: From fingertips down toward the elbows

explanation: Water should flow from cleanest (fingertips) to less clean (elbows) so dirty water never runs back down over your hands. [learn more](GST114_U2_T13#GST114_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why is it important for a primary health care nurse in a rural Nigerian community to understand seasonal disease patterns?

options.A: To accurately predict the winner of upcoming local political elections
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of imported medical equipment
options.C: To schedule annual leave during the busiest months of the year
options.D: To anticipate outbreaks like meningitis or cholera and prepare preventive supplies early

explanation: Brilliant! Knowing when seasonal illnesses like meningitis or cholera peak helps clinics stock up and protect the community on time. You're thinking like a true nurse! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h7)

question: What is the main focus of generalized anxiety disorder compared to neurasthenia?

options.A: Severe physical paralysis of the lower limbs
options.B: Excessive and uncontrollable worry about future events
options.C: Complete loss of memory regarding personal identity
options.D: Sudden bursts of intense physical energy

explanation: You got it! Anxiety is all about constant, runaway worry, whereas neurasthenia focuses on running out of nervous energy. Keep up the brilliant effort! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T9#GNS314_U2_T9_h5)

question: How does a concept differ from a variable in a research study?

options.A: A concept only appears in the conclusion section
options.B: A variable is never used in quantitative research
options.C: A variable is imaginary, while a concept is physical
options.D: A concept is an abstract idea, while a variable is measured

explanation: A concept is a broad mental thought (like 'pain' or 'anxiety'), but a variable is how you actually measure it in the study (like a pain scale score). [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h4)

question: What does "role ambiguity" mean for a nursing team on the ward?

options.A: Staff members refuse to speak to each other during shifts
options.B: There are not enough wheelchairs available for patients
options.C: The hospital building has confusing hallways and signs
options.D: Nurses are unclear about their exact duties and responsibilities

explanation: Role ambiguity happens when job boundaries are fuzzy. When nobody is quite sure who is supposed to handle a specific task, confusion and frustration naturally follow. [learn more](GST321_U5_T2#GST321_U5_T2_h2)

question: Why does high national debt servicing negatively affect public health budgets?

options.A: It directly increases the number of patients seeking private insurance
options.B: It forces international health organizations to withdraw all nursing staff
options.C: It automatically lowers the market price of essential pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: It drains government revenue that could otherwise be allocated to social sectors like health

explanation: When a huge chunk of national income goes to paying off debts, less money is left in the purse for hospitals, schools, and health programs. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h5)

question: A patient is given a drug that blocks parasympathetic activity. Which symptom would you most likely see?

options.A: Rapid digestion and frequent urination
options.B: Slowed heart rate and excessive drooling
options.C: Dry mouth and decreased bowel sounds
options.D: Constricted pupils and low blood pressure

explanation: The parasympathetic system is your 'rest-and-digest' mode. Blocking it stops secretions and slows the gut down, resulting in a dry mouth and sluggish digestion. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h4)

question: What tiny calcium stones help your brain sense gravity and straight-line movement?

options.A: Ossicles
options.B: Stereocilia
options.C: Otoliths
options.D: Cerumen

explanation: Think of otoliths as tiny natural 'ear stones' that shift with gravity over sensory cells, letting you know if you are standing up straight or leaning. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T2#GNS211_U4_T2_h6)

question: A busy ward has only one working patient lift, and both the day and night shifts keep arguing over who gets to use it. What is driving this conflict?

options.A: Personality clashes
options.B: Role ambiguity
options.C: Resource scarcity
options.D: Value differences

explanation: When important tools or equipment are in short supply, tension builds up fast. That is classic resource scarcity in action! [learn more](GST321_U5_T2#GST321_U5_T2_h2)
